editorial:
Imagine graduating from college and realizing your whole life is already planned out for you. That is exactly where Barry B. Benson finds himself. He is a young bee who wants more than just making honey for the rest of his days. After meeting a human florist named Vanessa, Barry learns that humans have been stealing honey from bees for years. Furious, he decides to sue the entire human race. The movie mixes silly humor with a surprisingly big adventure, and the world of bees is colorful and fun to explore. You will laugh at the ridiculous courtroom scenes and enjoy the friendship between Barry and Vanessa.

The voice acting is lively, especially from Jerry Seinfeld as Barry, and the animation still looks bright and cheerful. The pacing moves quickly, though some jokes land better than others, and the story gets a little wild toward the end. Still, it is a fun ride for kids and adults who enjoy goofy comedy. If you want to watch it, stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: Barry wins the lawsuit, and all the honey is returned to the bees. But without humans collecting honey, the bees stop working and flowers stop blooming. Barry realizes his mistake and helps return the honey to stores. He and Vanessa then work together to save the dying flowers by flying a plane full of pollen across the country. In the end, bees and humans learn to share, and Barry finally finds a job he loves as a pollen jockey.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves goofy animated comedies and family-friendly adventures.
